   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  June 3, 2024
 To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Councilmembers John Mirisch and
  Mary Wells
 From:  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
  Corrina Lesser, Recreation Supervisor
 Subject:  Festival Beverly Hills

 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
To provide a brief history for context, the Arts and Culture Commission proposed Festival
Beverly Hills as a signature Arts and Culture event for the community, and the inaugural
event was held on Sunday, March 12, 2023, at the Beverly Hills Farmers Market from
9:00am to 1:00pm. As part of responding to Council priorities for FY 2021-22, the Arts and
Culture Commission proposed the annual cultural festival, as a means of bringing the
community together around arts and culture. A community-wide survey had identified the
creation of the festival as a top priority. The inaugural Festival Beverly Hills included
performances and hands-on family friendly activities from more than 15 artists and
organizations including:

  •  Cultural performances and tutorials from organizations like the Asian Arts Dance
  Team, Blue13, Cortines High School, Self Help Graphics & Art, and Southern
  California Marimba
  •  Culinary programs with a teen cooking competition and an Iranian spice-making
  workshop
  •  Iconic Southern California-based organizations like Bob Baker Marionette Theatre,
  dublab Community Radio, LA Carnivale, and LA Commons
  •  Performances by Beverly Hills Unified School District music production and dance
  students

Festival Beverly Hills aims to celebrate and showcase the cultural diversity of the City of
Beverly Hills and Southern California. Through a wide range of performances, family-
friendly workshops, activities, as well as culinary offerings, Festival Beverly Hills
exemplifies the City as a world-class arts and cultural destination. The objective of the
Arts and Culture Commission and Community Services Department staff for the second
annual Festival Beverly Hills, is to build upon the success of the inaugural festival and
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024
continue to elevate Festival Beverly Hills as a cultural destination for both the Beverly Hills
community and the Greater Southern California region.

On January 30, 2024, the Arts and Culture Commission and Community Services Staff
asked then-Council Liaisons Mayor Dr. Julian M. Gold and Lili Bosse to support their
recommendation to make the following changes for the second annual Festival Beverly
Hills event:

  •  Hold Festival Beverly Hills in the summer, on either July 21 or July 28, 2024, in
  order to optimize talent acquisition and deploy a more robust marketing and
  promotional strategy
  •  Move the location of Festival Beverly Hills from the Beverly Hills Farmer’s Market
  to Roxbury Park, to build on the success of the first festival, and expand the
  footprint of the event

These recommendations were supported by the Arts and Culture Council Liaisons,
including the directive that the Commission and Community Services staff meet with the
liaisons at a future date, to provide a more detailed report in advance of the 2024
festival. City Council Liaisons also desired a robust marketing campaign for the 2024
festival, extended hours and expressed a willingness to consider budgetary requests to
support event promotion and other Festival expenses, if needed.

DISCUSSION
Since the date of the last Council Liaison meeting to discuss Festival Beverly Hills,
Community Services staff have continued meeting with the Arts and Culture Performing
Arts and Annual Events (Festival Beverly Hills) Ad Hoc Committee, Vice Chair Karla
Gordy Bristol and Commissioner Pamela Beck, to execute the goal of building upon the
success of the inaugural festival and incorporate the direction and recommendations
provided by the Council Liaisons and Ad Hoc Committee. To provide the more robust
details requested by the Council Liaisons, we are highlighting the event programming
and marketing strategy, confirmed partnerships, means for showcasing the cultural
diversity of the region, and budget outlook for the 2024 festival.

The second annual Festival Beverly Hills event will take place on Sunday, July 21 from
12pm – 6pm at Roxbury Park. The programming strategy developed for the event, was
based upon the direction of the Arts and Culture Commission Annual Events Ad Hoc
members Vice Chair Karla Gordy Bristol, Commissioner Lilliana Filipovic (replaced by
Commission Beck in March 2024), and Commissioner Pamela Beck (as of March 2024).
When Ad Hoc meetings commenced last fall, the committee articulated the following
priorities for the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills event:

  •  Engage consulates within the Los Angeles Consular Corps to participate
  •  Identify artists and festival elements that represent the demographics of Beverly
  Hills, along with Greater Southern California
  •  Include pop-up dance performances and elements of spectacle to engage
  participants throughout the festival

Featured programming elements for the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills include the following:

  •  Performances and programming will be featured on two performance stages, a
  Story Hub, and event space booths

Page 2 of 4
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024
  •  Representation from more than 13 cultures including Israeli, Indigenous/Aztec,
  Japanese, Mexican, Persian, Hawaiian/Polynesian, and Afro-Cuban, along with
  consular contributions from the countries of Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador,
  Senegal, and Tobago and Trinidad
  • Six dance performances from cultural and professional dance companies
  • Four musical performances from cultural and professional dance companies
  • Global DJ sets from community radio station dublab
  • A Story Hub featuring storytelling traditions from across cultures including poetry
  from organizations like Street Poets and Beyond Baroque and puppetry
  performances from Bob Baker Marionette Theater and the Farhang Foundation
  • Hands-on experiences including cultural arts and craft, contemplative art
  demonstrations like a traditional Japanese tea ceremony, and an opportunity to
  contribute to a community poem with a mobile recording booth
  • A record and book fair pop-up featuring global music and literary selections
  • A food truck hub and dining area featuring an array of global cuisines
Please note: Since the contracting process with planned artists and performers is at
various stages per performer, not all specific artists will be identified at this time.

The festival programming identified above fits within the allocated event budget of
$47,000 and can be absorbed within the Community Services budget. This is an
increase of $31,000 from the 2023 festival. The Arts and Culture Commission
Performing Arts and Annual Events Ad Hoc Committee has identified some additional
talent that could potentially be secured if additional funding was provided, at the
recommendation of the Council Liaisons. Notable artists that have been identified as
potential additions to the festival lineup range in cost from approximately $5,000 -
$15,000, based upon prior discussions with artists.

The marketing and promotional strategy will focus on the following to both inform the
local community, and expand event awareness around the Southern California region:
  • Festival Beverly Hills postcards distributed to local businesses, hotels, and at
  Community Services and City-wide summer events
  • Event signage posted at City parking garages
  • Digital advertising and event boosts on social media including Facebook and
  Instagram
  • Weekly social media campaigns leading up to the July 21 event including artist
  spotlights and a curated music playlist
  • Digital communications to Arts and Culture Division email lists that reach
  approximately 18,000 people (which has an open rate of 60%)
  • Digital and/or print advertising in both local and regional publications that feature
  event and cultural destinations across the region
  • Coordination with Festival partner organizations, artists, and food trucks to
  promote Festival Beverly Hills to their networks

FISCAL IMPACT
The costs for the expanded 2024 Festival Beverly Hills at $47,000 are allocated within the
current Community Services Department operating budget. If there is a desire this year,
or in the future, to expand programming even further beyond the currently-budgeted
expansion, additional funding will need to be approved by the full City Council. If there is
a desire to provide additional funding beyond the allocated festival budget of $47,000, staff
seeks direction from the Council Liaisons to determine the type of programming desired
and the corresponding additional funding that would be supported in order to present the
request to the full City Council.
Page 3 of 4
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024

RECOMMENDATION
The Arts and Culture Commission and staff recommend that the Arts and Culture
Council Liaisons discuss and support the proposed details of the program and provide
any additional recommendations for Festival Beverly Hills on July 21, 2024.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By

  Monday, June 3, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  June 3, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Councilmember John Mirisch, Councilmember Mary Wells, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Recreational Services Manager Matthew Brown, Director of
  Community Services Stephanie Harris, Arts and Culture Commission Vice
  Chair Karla Gordy Bristol

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Festival Beverly Hills:
  a. Presentation from Matthew Brown:
  i. The objectives for the second annual Festival Beverly Hills are to build
  upon the success of the inaugural festival and to continue to elevate
  Beverly Hills as a local and regional cultural event destination.
  ii. The last Liaison Meeting authorized the festival to move to July from March
  and to relocate from the Farmers Market to Roxbury Park.
  iii. The festival will feature two performance stages, a storytelling hub, a
  consulate concourse area, event booths, a global food truck/culinary area
  with dining spaces, cultural arts and crafts, art demonstrations, and poetry.
  iv. The commission placed a priority on engaging the LA consulate corps for
  participation in the festival.
  v. 13 different cultures will be present at the event.
  vi. There will also be record and book pop up stores located in the western
  pavilion.
  vii. Marketing for the event will consist of event postcards, promotional
  signage at city facilities & parking structures, digital advertisements, social
  media promotion, email blasts, digital and print advertising, and
  coordinated marketing with participating artists, performers, and
  organizations.
  viii. The festival programming comes in at $47,000, which is covered by the
  Community Services Operating Budget. Additional funding would require
  funding approval from the full council.
  ix. This is a $31,000 increase from the 2023 festival.
 Highlights for June 3, 2024
Arts and Culture Commission Committee

  b. Councilmember Wells is concerned that a summer event date would depress local
  attendance due to school not being in session.
  c. The Arts and Culture commission does not feel that the event occurring in the
  summer will depress attendance numbers because of conflict with summer plans
  with families on summer break due to their experiences with prior summer events.
  d. Both councilmembers’ Wells and Mirisch would prefer the event to be held in
  Beverly Gardens Park in order to better attract tourists as they view Roxbury Park
  as out of the way from visitors.
  e. Councilmember Mirisch would like to move the event to the fall if the goal is to
  attract locals and leave it in the summer if the goal is to attract tourists.
  f. Due to the event being next month there will be some difficulties with moving the
  events location or date such as promotional materials already being circulated as
  well as contracts already being signed for the event.
  g. The Commission will study moving the event to Beverly Gardens Park and get
  back to the Liaisons within the next week.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: June 3, 2024 / 3:48 PM
